dimension_1.justification: The design exhibits an exemplary layered architecture (API Presentation -> Service Business Logic -> Repository Data Access -> Model Entities, supplemented by Celery asynchronous workers). Layer dependencies are strictly unidirectional with zero circular references. Boundaries between ContentSubmission orchestration, ContentValidator pipeline logic, and Celery task execution are cleanly decoupled. Horizontally scalable patterns such as Redis-locked Celery Beat sweepers and PostgreSQL transaction advisory locks (pg_advisory_xact_lock) are applied thoughtfully to prevent concurrency races.

dimension_2.justification: API contracts follow RESTful conventions rigorously with comprehensive Pydantic v2 schemas across all endpoints. Proper HTTP status codes (200, 201, 403, 404, 409, 422) are documented with exact semantics. Pagination is properly implemented for list endpoints via PaginatedResponse, and standardized AppError mapping is specified. The agent covers the full end-to-end lifecycle corresponding to all required states (draft, submit, auto_check, brand review, revision request, resubmit, publish confirmation), exceeding the reference baseline while maintaining strict role-based authorization.

dimension_3.justification: The relational data model is complete and production-grade. The separation of mutable ContentSubmission and immutable ContentVersion entities correctly models snapshot history. All fields include concrete types, nullability, defaults, and foreign keys. Composite uniqueness on (submission_id, version_number) prevents version collision, and indexes are tailored to lookup patterns (status, application_id, status + updated_at). Standard mixins (TimestampMixin, SoftDeleteMixin) and PostgreSQL enums match established service patterns.

dimension_4.justification: Integration with existing modules (User, Campaign, Application) respects established patterns without introducing extraneous infrastructure. The design correctly leverages X-User-Id header auth, require_role dependencies, SQLAlchemy 2.0 asyncpg, Redis, and Celery. Integration contracts with internal repositories, in-memory sensitive word Trie scanning, Celery Beat periodic sweeps, and external Image Quality APIs include concrete timeout limits, circuit breakers, and graceful degradation strategies.

dimension_5.justification: All six architectural decisions include detailed trade-off analyses, evaluated alternatives, and performance rationales (e.g., choosing asynchronous Celery workers to preserve the sub-500ms p95 SLA against slow 10s external image APIs). Four distinct high-severity operational risks (worker starvation, version race conditions, Celery worker crashes in auto_checking, and dead CDN URLs) are identified with actionable, production-ready mitigations (Redis lock TTLs, acks_late/task_reject_on_worker_lost, watchdog sweeper, and HEAD reachability checks).

scores.overall_assessment: This is an exceptional, production-ready technical design that faithfully adheres to existing system patterns while expanding on the reference design with robust async validation, circuit breaking, and complete lifecycle coverage. It demonstrates senior-to-principal level domain modeling, concurrency management, and operational resilience.
